extracted.intended_audience: educational researchers, curriculum designers, cognitive scientists, and practicing teachers interested in learning theory and instructional design
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and assessing instruction that treats knowledge as situated — i.e., as produced and used within activity, context, and culture — with emphasis on cognitive apprenticeship and authentic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situated Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is not independent of situations; it is fundamentally 'situated,' being in part a product of the activity, context, and culture in which it is developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction and evaluation should assume that conceptual knowledge is co-produced with activity and context; avoid treating knowledge as wholly abstract transferable propositions. Example: technical concepts are always 'under construction' and inherit part of their meaning from situations of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning must involve authentic or domain-congruent activity — the ordinary activities of practitioners — because concepts acquire structure and meaning in those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks that are congruent with practitioners' ordinary work (not simplified or decontextualized classroom surrogates). Anti-pattern: 'ersatz' classroom tasks (e.g., many textbook word problems) that remove extraneous but essential contextual supports and thus distort what is learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enculturation (Entry into Practitioner Culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning is a process of enculturation: to use conceptual tools as practitioners do, students must enter the community and its cultural viewpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide opportunities to observe practitioners, participate in authentic practices, and gradually adopt community norms and perspectives (legitimate peripheral participation). Do not assume that presenting abstract concepts suffices for enculturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual Knowledge as Tools (Use-Based Understanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual knowledge should be treated like tools: it is fully understood in use, and mere acquisition of declarations or algorithms can leave knowledge inert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize teaching through use, demonstration, and practice in purpose-driven tasks; beware of teaching only definitions or routines that students cannot deploy in authentic situations (example: algorithmic competence without problem-solving ability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexicality and Context Dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Many elements of knowledge (like indexical words) depend completely on the situation for interpretation; replacing indexicals with elaborate descriptions changes transparency and can make understanding opaque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve or recreate contextual supports rather than compensating with verbose descriptions. Where indexical reference is essential, provide situational grounding (e.g., physical artifacts, shared context cues) rather than only abstract descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed Cognition (Environment and Social Structure as Cognitive Resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognition is often distributed across artifacts, the physical environment, and social collaborations; people off-load cognitive work onto these supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning situations that make use of artifacts, environmental structure, and collaboration as part of problem solving (examples: using measuring cups as part of a solution, crates as an embedded abacus). Evaluate whether tasks allow learners to exploit external supports rather than insisting on purely internal computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Apprenticeship — Modeling and Coaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should act as masters modeling authentic expert practices and thinking processes for novices, then coach learners through practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit modeling of strategies and thought processes, coached practice with fading support, and use of real tasks. Evaluate instruction on whether modeling makes tacit processes visible and coaching progressively transfers responsibility to learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Apprenticeship — Scaffolding, Articulation, Reflection, Exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective cognitive apprenticeship involves scaffolding, prompting learners to articulate reasoning, providing opportunities for reflection, and encouraging exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scaffolds are provided and then removed as competence grows; prompt students to make their reasoning explicit and to reflect on strategies; create structured opportunities for independent exploration. Figures in the paper emphasize 'apprenticeship–coaching–collaboration–multiple practice–reflection' and 'articulation/making apparent' as components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for Multiple Roles and Role-Display
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic tasks require many roles; groups allow display of multiple roles which an individual would struggle to perform simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use group-based activities to let learners enact different roles (e.g., analyst, recorder, critic) and thereby observe and discuss role-specific perspectives. Evaluate whether tasks permit role differentiation and role reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective Problem Solving (Group Synergy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups can produce synergistic insights and solutions that individual members would not reach alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor collaborative tasks that require integration of multiple viewpoints and cooperative reasoning. Assess group tasks for evidence of emergent solutions attributable to group interaction rather than mere aggregation of individual answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confronting Misconceptions through Social Interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Group interaction provides an efficient means to surface, confront, and discuss students' ineffective strategies and misconceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure activities and discussions to elicit students' underlying ideas so they can be examined publicly; use peer critique and instructor facilitation to resolve deep misconceptions rather than relying solely on corrective explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing Collaborative Work Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should cultivate skills needed for collaborative work, since workplace and many authentic contexts require joint problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and assess norms for collaboration (communication, coordination, shared responsibility) through repeated group practice; evaluate students both on domain tasks and on their collaborative competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in Authentic Contexts for Situated Generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrent practice in authentic activity (practice across multiple real contexts) builds generalizable, though situated, knowledge rather than abstract, decontextualized rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide varied authentic contexts for applying a concept so learners develop texture and robustness in understanding. Avoid narrow practice limited to classroom cues that do not appear in real settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage, Don’t Dismiss, Students' Inventive Heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Students bring context-sensitive heuristics and inventive strategies from everyday problem solving that schools often dismiss unnecessarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicit students' heuristics, validate and adapt productive ones for domain tasks (example: grouping strategies in multiplication), and build instruction that uses learners' inventiveness rather than penalizing nonstandard approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Over-explication That Removes Useful Implicit Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A common mistake is making implicit, context-bound constraints fully explicit, which can create inappropriate ontological commitments and hamper learning efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide carefully which aspects of practice to make explicit and which to leave implicit/indexical. Excessive explication may produce brittle learning; prefer situated exemplars and guided participation over exhaustive conceptual formalization when the context does the indexing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Assessments and Tasks to Preserve Contextual Supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks and assessments should preserve or simulate the extralinguistic and situational supports learners use in authentic practice; removing these supports makes learning fragile and nontransferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating problems or exams, include the contextual cues and artifacts that practitioners would use (or assess in situ) rather than relying on abstracted textbook formats that teach only school-specific cues (anti-pattern: math word problems with unrealistic constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and Counteract School-Culture Distortion
rubrics_metrics.description: Schooling often produces a pervasive culture with its own tasks, cues, and evaluation norms that can be antithetical to authentic domain learning and hinder transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether classroom practices privilege school-specific signposts (e.g., textbook position cues) and redesign instruction and assessment to align more closely with domain practices and purposes so success in school predicts performance outside it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Social Narrative and Circulation for Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Social interaction and the circulation of narrative within groups support enculturation and the sharing of practice-relevant knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage group storytelling, reflection about approaches taken, and the sharing of narratives of problem solving as part of instruction; assess whether narratives circulate and inform subsequent practice.
